PullRequest.Title: sessions: Find sessions by pull request number

Addresses #338901

## Summary

Adds associated GitHub pull request numbers to the Agents window Sessions view Find labels.

- Matches pull requests exposed by workspace GitHub metadata, including the legacy single-PR shape.
- Matches recorded GitHub pull request artifacts and references.
- Accepts searches with or without the `#` prefix.

External sessions whose catalog does not yet expose pull request metadata remain follow-up work tracked by #338901.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Pre-commit hygiene for both changed files — passed.
- Code OSS Dev UI scenario on macOS ARM64, version 1.141.0 — passed: searching `#241533` left only the associated session visible while the number was absent from session titles.
- Focused Electron unit test command was attempted earlier, but Electron exited with `SIGSEGV` before executing tests in the sandboxed environment.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: `FindController.applyPattern` synchronously refilters on each input, `FindFilter.filter` invokes the label provider once per candidate node, and the sessions list explicitly removes per-group caps while a find pattern is active. The exact history size varies by user, which affects severity, but the synchronous repeated mechanism and scaling are directly traced.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU regex/URI serialization work and short-lived arrays, strings, and parsed PR objects.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For every typed character or edited query, cost grows as O(searchable sessions × (workspace PR refs + session artifacts)); active find removes the normal per-group cap, and there is no cold/warm distinction because labels are rebuilt on every lookup.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased synchronous input latency and CPU/GC pressure during session filtering.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Each candidate lookup returned `element.title.get()` directly, so a refilter performed only title fuzzy matching and did not walk folders/artifacts, serialize URIs, run PR regexes, or allocate a label array per session.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each label lookup now reconstructs all searchable labels from mutable session metadata and parses every GitHub pull-request artifact instead of returning the already-stored title string.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT lines 347-366 add a helper that rebuilds an array, walks every folder/PR and artifact, serializes artifact URIs, and regex-parses PR URLs; RIGHT line 3838 replaces the prior `element.title.get()` label with this helper on the tree label-provider path.
Findings.Title: Cache PR labels before the synchronous find loop
Findings.Impact: Typing in Sessions Find can become progressively laggy and create CPU/GC pressure for users with a large session history or artifact-heavy sessions; ordinary title searches pay the PR extraction cost even when the query contains no PR number.
Findings.Evidence: The new helper creates `labels` and `#number` strings on every invocation, calls `getGitHubPullRequestRefs` for each folder (which additionally allocates a legacy ref object/array), and calls `artifact.link.toString(true)` plus `parseGitHubPullRequestUrl` for each eligible artifact. `abstractTree.ts` invokes this provider from `FindFilter.filter`, and `FindController.applyPattern` calls `tree.refilter()` for every input value. `sessionsList.ts` also sets `hasFindPattern` and rebuilds the tree without workspace/group limits once text is entered, so the work covers the full searchable history rather than the usual five-item capped groups.
Findings.Recommendation: Memoize the derived label array per session (for example with a WeakMap-backed observable/derived value) and invalidate it when title, workspace GitHub metadata, or artifacts change, so each metadata version is parsed once rather than once per keystroke while preserving live updates.

Scenarios.Scenario: Filter Sessions by title or pull-request number in the Find widget
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each find input fires `onDidChangeValue`, synchronously updates the pattern, rebuilds the uncapped tree when find first becomes active, and calls `tree.refilter`; every candidate session must finish label extraction and fuzzy matching before filtering and input handling complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize artifact `URI` values and parse canonical GitHub PR URLs while constructing search labels.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One local URI serialization and regex parse for each eligible PR artifact of every searchable session on every query edit; workspace PR labels are also rebuilt per folder/ref. Active find bypasses normal per-group limits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The label provider returned the stored title string and performed no URI serialization or PR parsing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All serialization/parsing completes inside the synchronous refilter before the filtered tree is available.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of sessions in the full searchable history after find removes group caps, multiplied by folders/PR refs and artifacts per session, then by query edits.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entirely synchronous and serial on the UI thread; one label-provider invocation per candidate session, with nested serial loops over folders, PR refs, and artifacts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no cache for derived navigation labels: cold and warm queries both rebuild arrays and PR strings and reparse artifact URLs. Existing session observables expose invalidation points, but the changed callback reads and recomputes them on every lookup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the framework call path, synchronous refilter, cap bypass, and added loops/allocations are explicit in repository code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact session/artifact histories and milliseconds vary by user; the uncapped all-session multiplicity and per-keystroke synchronous placement are established, so uncertainty affects severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium repeated-work regression: the feature correctly expands searchable metadata but reparses stable metadata on every keystroke, including textual title searches.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type-to-navigate while focus is in the Sessions tree
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The list type-navigation controller loops synchronously until it finds a matching row or exhausts the current flattened list; each scanned session now performs metadata extraction before keyboard focus can move.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Rebuild navigation labels and serialize/parse PR artifact URLs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one URI serialization/parse per eligible PR artifact for each scanned session on each type-navigation input.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each scanned session exposed only its title string with no metadata traversal or serialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly delays keyboard focus navigation until a match is found or the list is exhausted.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of flattened rows scanned before a match, multiplied by session metadata size and typed characters.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous serial scan on the UI thread with early termination on a match; worst-case cardinality is the full current flattened list.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No label cache is used; each navigation key sequence recomputes labels for every scanned item, though the scan can stop at the first match.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for execution and scaling; lower magnitude than Find because matching can terminate early and collapsed nodes reduce cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The current flattened list is often reduced by collapsed sections or group caps, so this path is generally smaller than active Find; large expanded/date-grouped lists can still expose the repeated work.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the same reported mechanism; no separate finding because it shares the same changed callback and has lower effective cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render title highlighting for matches found through alternate PR labels
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After filtering, only rendered session rows call `getSessionTitleMatches`; it compares the matched label with the current title and creates highlight ranges when appropriate.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of visible rendered session rows, not total session history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous rendering of virtualized visible rows; no fan-out beyond rendered templates.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Filter data carries the matched label and score only for the current refilter; rendered title matches are not persistently cached, but rendering is virtualized.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that this renderer path is bounded and introduces no external or serialization boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Visible row count and rerender frequency vary, but the added comparison/allocation is bounded by viewport virtualization and is small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate performance regression: the changed renderer work is small, synchronous, and viewport-bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Traced Find and type-navigation callbacks through tree refiltering, cap removal, rendering, and local serialization; submitted one medium-confidence-severity finding for repeated per-keystroke PR label reconstruction. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operations are reached by the changed paths, and the renderer adaptation is viewport-bounded.
